title: The black stone on a cloak
hookLine: the clans of Mecca nearly come to blows over who will lift the Black Stone, and he lays it on a cloak so every clan lifts together

lines: THE KA'BA REBUILT, WALL BY WALL.
cards: Every group project has this moment: the work is almost done, and suddenly everyone wants the part that gets the credit. In Mecca, around the time the Prophet ﷺ was thirty-five, the Ka'ba had been damaged.
The clans of Quraysh tore it down to its foundations and rebuilt it together, each clan taking a wall.
All went well until the last step: setting the Black Stone, the ancient stone in the Ka'ba's corner, back in its place. Every clan wanted the honor. Nobody would back down.

teach.h: HANDS IN A BOWL OF BLOOD.
teach.b: Ibn Ishaq tells it. Some clans even dipped their hands in a bowl of blood and swore to fight.

teach.h: THE NEXT MAN THROUGH THE GATE.
teach.b: The oldest man there suggested: let the next man who walks through the gate of the sanctuary decide, and we'll all accept it. They agreed.
The next man through the gate was the young man they called al-Amin, and they were relieved: it's the trustworthy one, we accept him. He asked for a cloak.
He spread it on the ground and set the Black Stone in the middle with his own hands. Then: let each clan's leader take hold of a corner.
They lifted it together, all of them, up to its place, and he set the stone into the wall. No clan won.

teach.h: A CLOAK, AND EVERY CLAN LIFTS.
teach.b: Every clan carried. The man who solved it didn't take the honor for himself; he shared it out.
Today Muslims walking around the Ka'ba on pilgrimage kiss the Black Stone, or touch it, or simply raise a hand toward it from the crowd. But it isn't worshiped.

A well-known report in Sahih al-Bukhari has 'Umar, a leading companion, saying to the stone: I know you're only a stone, you can neither harm nor help; if I hadn't seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss you, I wouldn't kiss you.
The Qur'an asks believers, in Pickthall's words: “hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate.”
And that closes week twelve: a valley of idols, an elephant, an orphan, three homes, a trust, a merchant who saw him first, and a cloak with four corners.

how: Pilgrims begin each circuit of the Ka'ba at the Black Stone, kissing or touching it if they can reach it, or raising a hand toward it from a distance; Muslims honor it as a stone the Prophet kissed, not as an object of worship.

o: a stone idol the clans of Mecca worshiped
the first stone of the wall each clan built
the ancient corner stone set back in the Ka'ba

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: each wanted to set the stone
the next man through the gate
every clan leader took a corner
I know you're only a stone

s: 'Umar said: I know you're only a stone; I kiss you because I saw the Prophet kiss you (Bukhari).
the Prophet set the stone in the wall himself, after the clans lifted it together
the clans agreed to let a religious leader decide
they agreed to let the next man through the gate decide, and it was him.

games.q: you've been chosen to settle it. every clan wants the honor of setting the Black Stone, and they're ready to fight. what do you do?
o: set it in place yourself and end the argument.
lay it on a cloak and have every clan lift a corner.
games.why: he spreads a cloak, sets the stone on it, and every clan's leader lifts a corner; then he places it with his own hands.

practice: Think of one standoff in your life right now, who does the dishes, who hosts the holidays, who gets credit on the team, and picture everyone involved standing around it.
Look for the cloak: one idea, not a perfect one, that lets each person hold a corner, so nobody wins and nobody loses. If you pray, you can ask Allah for a way through.

wordCard.voice: Black Stone. The clans nearly fight over this corner stone of the Ka'ba, until it's set on a cloak so all of them can lift it together.

orig.note: Arabic: the Black Stone, set in the eastern corner of the Ka'ba.

carryVoice: Your line: everyone takes a corner. Tomorrow, he climbs to a cave to be alone. Twelve weeks on the path, done.
